The primary PR you're looking for is **[#11845 "Implement re-lexing logic for better error recovery"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/11845)** by dhruvmanila. This PR implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing.

Key implementation details:
- It reduces the nesting level by 1. It shouldn't reset it to 0 because otherwise the recovery from nested list parsing will be incorrect.

The related issue **[#11916 "Improve error recovery for strings and f-strings"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/11916)** explains the underlying problem with the logical token / non-logical newline handling:

- There's more to f-strings than a normal string literal because it can contain an expression element. This means that there could be an unterminated f-string or the closing curly brace could be missing or an error in the expression itself.
- Currently, the parser drops all unterminated strings, or more precisely the lexer doesn't emit the string token for unterminated strings. This is for both normal and formatted string literals.

- A remaining complication: The parser doesn't use existing list parsing logic for parsing comma-separated expressions aka tuple expression which means it doesn't benefit from any error recovery logic. Thus, if there's an error in the f-string expression itself, there's a high chance it'll not recover correctly.

## Broader Context

This work fits into the tracking issue **[#10653 "Error recovery improvements for the new parser"](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/10653)**, which followed Ruff's move to a hand-written parser. As noted in the v0.4.0 announcement, a hand-written parser also opens the door to future optimizations and improvements, especially in error recovery.

I found several relevant results related to Ruff's re-lexing logic, f-string handling, and error recovery. Here's a summary of the key pull requests and issues by dhruvmanila and others:

## The Core Re-lexing PR (#11845)

The foundational work is "Implement re-lexing logic for better error recovery" by dhruvmanila, which implements the re-lexing logic in the parser. This logic is only applied when recovering from an error during list parsing. One notable discussion point was the `re_lex_logical_token` snapshot test, where reviewers debated whether to map NonLogicalNewline to newline, since it seemed an odd error message to show to users.

## Line Continuation Bug Fix (#12008)

A follow-up fix addressed a bug in the re-lexing logic. This PR fixes a bug where the re-lexing logic didn't consider the line continuation character being present before the newline character. This meant that the lexer was being moved back to the newline character which is actually ignored via the backslash.

The problem manifested with code like `f'middle {'string':\ 'format spec'}`, where the ranges were overlapping between the FStringMiddle token and the tokens emitted after moving the lexer backwards.

## Related Follow-up Issue (#12036)

An additional edge case was identified afterward: even with the earlier fix, the line continuation character could be part of a comment, meaning the newline character isn't being escaped. This won't create a panic but the lexer won't be moved back and keeps the NonLogicalNewline token instead of changing it to a Newline token.

## Background: FStringMiddle Token (#7042)

The `FStringMiddle` token was introduced as part of PEP 701 support. It's defined as the token value that includes the portion of text inside the f-string that's not part of the expression part and isn't an opening or closing brace.
